newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP condemns annulment of Serbian election results.
newsitem.headline: EP condemns annulment of Serbian election results.

text.p: The European Parliament on Wednesday condemned the Serbian authorities for annulling the results of the November 17 local elections and urged the European Union not to offer Serbia preferential trade terms.

In a strongly worded statement, the EU's directly elected assembly expressed deep concern about developments in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, including the silencing of independent media and the overturning of the election results.
The 626-member Parliament demanded that the Belgrade authorities respect the elections and launch a full inquiry into the alleged irregulities in conducting the poll.

The Euro-deputies' statement echoes a similar call from EU foreign ministers, who on December 6 postponed a decision to offer rump Yugoslavia -- Serbia and Montenegro -- preferential trade terms already granted to other Balkan states.

Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, who chaired the December 6 meeting, told Euro-MPs on Wednesday the ministers wanted rump Yugoslavia to rejoin the international community, "for the sake of prosperity and stability in the region".
"But it cannot do so unless it observes basic standards of democracy and human rights," he insisted.

"The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia's attitude towards the issues of respect for human and minority rights, and the observance of democratic norms, will be key factors in determining the Union's future relations with that country," Spring told the Parliament.

In their resolution, which is non-binding, the Euro-MPs insisted that "counteracting developments towards democray -- of which free elections and a free media are a fundamental part -- cannot be accepted by the Union".

The EU should not develop closer relations with Yugoslavia until the Serbs helped apprehend indicted war criminals on their territory and acted to reduce tension over the Serb-governed Kosovo region, the EU Parliament said.

Students and the opposition have been campaigning against Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic in the streets of Belgrade since Zajedno, the opposition coalition, accused the ruling Socialists of robbing it of victory in the local elections.

Carl Bildt, the international high representative in Bosnia, told a news conference on December 6, "In my opinion there will be no further deliberations on the question of preferential trade arrangements until the local elections issue has been sorted out."
